disclaimer: Injury statuses reflect training camp/preseason reports as of Aug. 20, 2026 (evening update). New this run: 49ers RB Christian McCaffrey added as questionable with leg/calf tightness - hasn't practiced since Aug. 10, HC Kyle Shanahan says he'd play in a regular-season week but the team is being cautious given his 2024 injury history. All other tracked situations (Kittle, Bosa, Evans, Pearsall, Higgins, Biadasz, Warren, Kamara, Pinter, LaPorta, and the rest) confirmed unchanged after a fresh check of tonight's preseason-game news, nfl.com/injuries, and insider (Schefter/Rapoport) searches - no roster moves affected tracked players. Pre-season camp/PUP-list information, not an official in-season practice-participation report - verify and update once real weekly injury reports are available.

injury.note: Passed his physical and was activated off the PUP list; practiced Aug. 10 for the first time this camp. On track to start at safety in Seattle's Sept. 9 season opener vs. New England.

Hasn't practiced since Aug. 10 with what the team calls general 'tightness'; per Ian Rapoport it's real, not a hold-in, though the exact muscle/tendon hasn't been specified. HC Kyle Shanahan says McCaffrey 'would play today' if it were a regular-season week and the team is just being cautious given his 2024 history, when a similar calf issue spiraled into a lost season (4 games, 50 carries). No firm return timetable yet.

Suffered in the 49ers' Jan. 11 playoff win over the Eagles. Opened training camp on the PUP list; GM John Lynch says the rehab is 'coming tremendous.' Kittle himself said this week he's been back running routes and likes his chances of being ready for Week 1, though he stressed he won't rush back before doctors clear him.

GM John Lynch announced Pearsall will have surgery on his PCL and is out for the entire 2026 season; placed on injured reserve. Recurring swelling in the same knee had limited him to two camp practices. 49ers re-signed Deebo Samuel in response.

Left Tuesday's (Aug. 18) joint practice with the Chargers early with tightness - initially had his foot/ankle iced before it was described as quad-related. HC Kyle Shanahan called it precautionary ('nothing I'm worried about right now'), coming right after Evans had returned to full practice Aug. 15 from the quad strain that sidelined him since Aug. 3. Still no firm return-to-full-practice timetable; recurring tightness in the same leg is a mild yellow flag to monitor.

Dealing with tendinitis in the knee he had surgically repaired for a torn ACL in 2025; not practicing and considered 'week-to-week' by HC Kyle Shanahan, who called the tendinitis a normal part of ACL recovery seen in roughly 90% of players. Goal remains for Bosa to play Week 1 vs. the Rams on Sept. 10.

injury.type: Hyperextended left knee, bone bruise, small fracture - underwent surgery
injury.note: HC Ben Johnson announced Aug. 11 that Bryant underwent knee surgery and will now miss 4-6 months, a significant setback from the initial 8-10 week outlook (surgery wasn't originally expected). Bears remain hopeful he could be available if Chicago makes the playoffs. Was Chicago's marquee free-agent addition this offseason (3-year, $40M deal).

Opened training camp on the PUP list with a calf injury that also sidelined him for OTAs and minicamp. GM Ryan Poles said Aug. 6 there's been a frustrating 'delay' in his recovery with no firm return timetable; Gordon says he believes he'll be ready soon.

Hurt getting tangled up with CB Tyrique Stevenson on the final rep of red-zone one-on-ones. Expected to miss the rest of the preseason (about a month) but the Bears believe he'll be ready for the Sept. 13 opener at Carolina. Poised for a bigger role after the DJ Moore trade to Buffalo; caught 47 passes for 652 yards and 2 TDs as a rookie in 2025.

Hurt getting tangled up with DT Grady Jarrett during an Aug. 16 practice. Initial tests suggested the knee was structurally sound, but a follow-up MRI confirmed the hyperextension and the Bears expect him to miss multiple weeks - possibly Week 1. In line for a bigger role behind the injury-prone D'Andre Swift.

injury.type: Ruptured patellar tendon (right knee) - surgically repaired
injury.note: Suffered in the Panthers' January playoff loss to the Rams; underwent surgery to repair the tendon. Rehab is reportedly "ahead of schedule" and the Panthers are "really feeling good" about his progress, per team reporting. On PUP to open camp; GM Dan Morgan remains optimistic he can return at some point this season.
Non-contact tear suffered on the first day of training camp practice — out for the season. The injury happened during the mandatory acclimation period, which the NFLPA is investigating.

Diagnosed with a blood clot in his lung in late June and placed on the reserve/non-football injury (NFI) list; immediately started on blood thinners and is reportedly responding well to treatment. Expected to miss the start of the regular season, per ESPN, though the team believes he could return at some point during the year.

Felt something grab during one-on-ones Wednesday and was sent for an MRI; HC Dave Canales called him week-to-week. Canales says he's confident Hubbard will be ready for Game 1, though the team isn't rushing him. Backup Jonathon Brooks is seeing expanded preseason reps in the meantime.

Carted off during Cincinnati's first padded/11-on-11 practice with a hyperextended knee; follow-up testing showed no ligament damage. Coach Zac Taylor confirmed Aug. 7 he'll be out 'several weeks' but is expected back well before the regular season ends.

MRI results (Aug. 19) confirmed a sprained MCL after Kamara left Tuesday's joint practice vs. Dallas; he avoided a more serious structural tear. Expected to be sidelined at least a month, which would put his return around mid-to-late September - likely missing the Sept. 13 opener at San Francisco and possibly Week 2 as well.

Got hit in the hip during practice this week and it flared up/became aggravated; HC Dan Campbell said Detroit will rest him to let it calm down and is unsure if he'll be ready for the Sept. 13 opener vs. New Orleans. LaPorta had surgery last November for a herniated disk but wasn't feeling lingering pain before this new issue; team says it feels good about his long-term outlook.

Suffered a season-ending torn ACL during Tuesday's joint practice with the Raiders, falling awkwardly on a red-zone route in 11-on-11 drills. The 2025 second-round pick started 10 games as a rookie (525 yards, 6 TDs); Houston will lean more on Xavier Hutchinson, Tank Dell and Jaylin Noel in his absence.

injury.type: Left leg injury (no structural damage) - recovered
injury.note: Returned to full practice and 11-on-11 team drills Monday, Aug. 17, after missing most of the prior week following a leg injury suffered tangling feet with WR Ja'Kobi Lane. HC Jesse Minter called the return a positive sign; Wiggins is set to be available for joint practices with Minnesota later this week.

Returned to full practice and 11-on-11 team drills Monday, Aug. 17, after a groin issue sidelined him for several days. HC Jesse Minter said Humphrey bounced back well; on track for Baltimore's joint practices with Minnesota later this week.

Suffered the injury during Wednesday's joint practice with the Vikings in Eagan, Minnesota, and was carted off in a full-leg brace; expected to miss the season. Was taking most first-team center reps in camp after Tyler Linderbaum's offseason move to the Raiders. Ethan Pocic and Jovaughn Gwyn are now the leading options to fill the void.

Left Wednesday's joint practice vs. Atlanta clutching his groin and did not return; HC Shane Steichen confirmed the injury. Per NFL insider Jordan Schultz, the Colts avoided a critical injury — Warren is expected to be out roughly a week, not weeks — though he'll be shut down for the rest of camp/preseason as a precaution. Second-year first-round pick coming off a strong rookie season (76 catches, 817 yards, 5 total TDs) and expected to be a lead target for Daniel Jones; trending toward being ready for the regular season.
Originally hurt in an October 2024 collision with Derrick Henry. Placed on reserve/PUP for a second straight season; not expected to play in 2026.

Recovering from left knee ACL surgery on Nov. 25. Limited to individual/7-on-7 work, not yet cleared for 11-on-11s; reportedly could be another ~4 weeks from full clearance and 'probably won't' play Week 1.

Carted off during an 11-on-11 period at Tuesday's practice; an MRI later that evening confirmed a torn ACL, per The Athletic's Josh Kendall. The 2025 first-round pick (No. 15 overall) will miss the entire 2026 season.

Hurt during minicamp; opened camp on PUP, no surgery required. Steelers Depot's Mark Kaboly said Aug. 7 he 'wouldn't anticipate' Ramsey practicing at all during camp, but spotted him doing field work alongside Joey Porter Jr. on Aug. 10, calling it 'good news' - a positive sign, though still no timetable for a return to full practice. HC Mike McCarthy said Aug. 19 he 'wouldn't say concern' about the continued absence, adding both Ramsey and Porter are 'making progress'; next game appearance may come at the Sept. 13 season opener vs. the Jets.

Rookie first-round pick (No. 3 overall) hurt his ankle late in Arizona's preseason game vs. the Raiders after a goal-line catch; expected to miss the rest of the preseason. Coach Mike LaFleur hasn't given a long-term prognosis, but the team is hopeful he's available for the Sept. 13 season opener vs. the Chargers.

Missed his 8th consecutive practice Tuesday (Aug. 18); HC Jim Harbaugh said Slater is working 'off to the sides' and expects him back this weekend. Will miss Thursday's preseason game vs. the 49ers. Slater has downplayed the issue ('nothing crazy'), but the absence has stretched well beyond the original veteran-rest-day framing - worth continuing to monitor given his 2025 patellar tendon tear.

injury.type: ACL damage + additional left knee injuries
injury.note: Hurt when a 49ers defensive lineman fell into his leg during Tuesday's joint practice; out indefinitely, per Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport. Signed with the Chargers in March on a 3-year, $30M deal after playing for Washington last season; will see more doctors for further clarity on the injury.

Suffered a torn ACL plus meniscus repair in Week 15 last season vs. Denver. Opened camp on PUP (July 29) and is expected to start the regular season there too, which would force him to miss at least the first four games. On Aug. 10, Parsons told NFL Network his 'most optimistic' return is Week 6 (Oct. 18, SNF vs. his old team the Cowboys at Lambeau), but stressed there's no guarantee given the Packers' internal recovery protocol for ACL-plus injuries.

New to Green Bay's camp injury report in early August with a sprained foot. Coach Matt LaFleur says he's hopeful Reed will be ready for the Sept. 7 season opener vs. Detroit, though the team is proceeding cautiously with the soft-tissue issue.
Returned to practice July 29 after a mild hamstring strain; fully participated with no limitations in Sunday's (Aug. 9) public training camp practice. On track for Week 1 vs. Chicago.

Hurt in a one-on-one pass-rush rep vs. Odafe Oweh during Saturday's practice; underwent surgery to repair the torn triceps. HC Dan Quinn didn't disclose an exact timeline, but recovery from this type of injury typically runs 4-7 months, likely sidelining him for most if not all of the 2026 season. Washington moved Brandon Coleman to left tackle in his place, with Andrew Wylie as depth; Quinn said the team isn't looking outside the building for additional O-line help.

Strained lifting weights ahead of camp; placed on PUP list on the first day of training camp. Traded to Philadelphia from Minnesota in April 2026 on a 4-year, $100M deal. DC Vic Fangio said Aug. 11 that Greenard is expected to miss at least a 'couple more weeks,' pushing him past all of training camp, though the injury is still not considered a long-term concern.

Back at practice this week in a limited/individual-drills capacity as the Eagles ramp him up ahead of joint sessions with New England; team says the hamstring issue is not serious and there's no long-term concern, though a firm return-to-full timetable still hasn't been set.

Recovering from a torn ACL/meniscus suffered in Week 4 last season vs. the Chargers, plus a follow-up spring surgery to clear scar tissue. Practiced for a second straight day Aug. 19 - in shells, taking team reps and catching passes in 7-on-7 - after his first live reps of camp Aug. 17. HC John Harbaugh says Nabers still needs to "get bumped around and hit" in practice before being considered for game action; not yet committed to Week 1 (Sept. 13 vs. Dallas), though the trajectory looks positive.

Suffered the injury Dec. 14, 2025 vs. the Chargers, ending his 2025 season; had knee debridement surgery in May. Fully cleared off the PUP list for camp and has been a full practice participant, including 11-on-11 team drills, since late July.
